2027-06-08.title: Tuesday of the Tenth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: For in him every one of God's promises is a “Yes.”
Lord, let your face shine on me
You are the salt of the earth … You are the light of the world
2027-06-08.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 10 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. A Mass of the Blessed Virgin Mary or another votive Mass may be chosen on a weekday without a memorial.
2027-06-08.verse: In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
theo: Paul had promised the Corinthians a visit and then changed his plans. Some of them said at once: you see, he is a man who says yes and no in the same breath; how can we trust his gospel? Paul answers the accusation, but he lifts it to a much higher level. His own travel plans may change; God's word does not. “As surely as God is faithful, our word to you has not been ‘Yes and No.’ For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we proclaimed among you, Silvanus and Timothy and I, was not ‘Yes and No’; but in him it is always ‘Yes.’” Then comes one of the great sentences of the New Testament: “For in him every one of God's promises is a ‘Yes.’ For this reason it is through him that we say the ‘Amen,’ to the glory of God.” Every promise God made to Abraham, to Moses, to David and to the prophets finds its fulfilment in Jesus. He is God's Yes to the world. And when the Church answers at the end of the Eucharistic Prayer with the great Amen, she is saying her own yes through him. Then Paul uses words that the Church has always heard as a description of Baptism and Confirmation: “But it is God who establishes us with you in Christ and has anointed us, by putting his seal on us and giving us his Spirit in our hearts as a first installment.” Anointed, sealed, given the Spirit as a first installment, a pledge of the full inheritance to come. The Catechism (1296) quotes exactly these words when it explains the seal of Confirmation. The Psalm, a verse from the long praise of God's law, prays like a disciple who has tasted that faithfulness: “The unfolding of your words gives light; it imparts understanding to the simple,” and “Make your face shine upon your servant.”

Yesterday Jesus spoke the Beatitudes. Today he tells the same people, the poor, the meek, the persecuted, who they are: “You are the salt of the earth.” “You are the light of the world.” He does not say: try to become salt, or one day you may be light. He says: you are. It is a gift before it is a task. Salt in the ancient world preserved food from going bad and gave it taste; it was also used with sacrifices and in making covenants. A little salt changes a whole dish. But “if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored? It is no longer good for anything.” Light is useless if it is hidden: “No one after lighting a lamp puts it under the bushel basket, but on the lampstand, and it gives light to all in the house.” Every Kerala home knows this. When the monsoon storms cut the electricity, someone lights the nilavilakku or a kerosene lamp and sets it in the middle of the room, not under the cot. Jesus' last word explains the purpose of the light: “so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.” Our good works are not meant to make people admire us but to make them praise God. The disciple is like the moon, which has no light of its own but reflects the sun. Paul's “Yes” in Christ and Jesus' salt and light belong together: the Christian sealed by the Spirit is God's Yes made visible in a village, an office, a classroom.
outline: Ask: have you ever made a promise and failed to keep it? How did it feel to the other person?
Every promise of God is fulfilled in Jesus, and through him we say Amen.
Baptism and Confirmation give us the Spirit as a first installment of heaven.
Jesus tells his disciples what they are, and why the lamp must not be hidden.
live: At your next Mass, say the great Amen at the end of the Eucharistic Prayer slowly and with your whole heart.
Put the lamp on the stand (Matthew 5:15)
Do one good work today openly and simply, not for praise, so that someone may thank God.
2027-06-08.prayer: Faithful God, in your Son Jesus Christ every one of your promises is Yes. We thank you for anointing us, for setting your seal upon us and giving us your Spirit in our hearts. Keep us from being people of yes and no, who promise and do not keep their word. Lord Jesus, you call us the salt of the earth and the light of the world; do not let us lose our taste or hide our light. Let our good works shine, so that all who see them may give glory to our Father in heaven. Amen.
altar: At the end of the Eucharistic Prayer the priest lifts the Body and Blood of Christ and sings: through him, and with him, and in him, all glory and honour is yours, almighty Father. The whole people answers: Amen. This is the Amen Paul speaks of, said through Christ to the glory of God. It is the most important Amen of the Mass: our yes to the Son who is God's Yes to us.

quick: Paul's travel plans changed, but God's word does not: in Jesus Christ every promise of God is a Yes, and through him we say Amen.
God has anointed us, put his seal on us and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a first installment, words the Church reads of Baptism and Confirmation.
Jesus tells his disciples: you are the salt of the earth and the light of the world; let your light shine so that others give glory to the Father.
2027-06-08.action: Keep one promise today that you have been postponing, and keep it fully.
2027-06-08.question: Is my light on the lampstand, or have I hidden it under a basket out of fear or laziness?

family.explain: Jesus said to his friends: you are salt and you are light. Salt makes food tasty and keeps it from spoiling. Light helps people see. Christians are meant to make the world better and to help people see God. When we do good things, people should not say: how good they are! but: how good God is!
family.intention: We pray for families without electricity or shelter during the heavy rains, and for all who keep their promises when it is hard.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is a light for our family? How can each of us be a little lamp at home this week?”

illus: During a heavy monsoon night in a village near Thrissur, the power failed and the whole lane went dark. In one house a grandmother, who had lit the nilavilakku every evening for sixty years, simply brought the lamp from the prayer corner and set it on the table in the front room, with the door open. Neighbours who were stumbling about with torches whose batteries were dying came and sat on her veranda. Someone started a hymn; somebody else brought tea. Her grandson remembered later that nobody talked about the grandmother that night; they talked about how good it was to be together and to pray. The lamp was not hidden, and the glory went to God. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Faithful God, your Yes in Christ never changes. Seal us again with your Spirit and make us salt and light for the people around us. Amen.
share: In him every one of God's promises is a Yes (2 Corinthians 1:20). Which promise of God do I most need to trust today?
God has put his seal on us and given us his Spirit (2 Corinthians 1:22). Do I live as someone sealed and anointed by God?
You are the light of the world (Matthew 5:14). Where is my light hidden, at home, at work or in my parish?
pm.resp: Lord, let your face shine on me.
interc: For the Church, that her members may be salt and light in a world that has lost its taste for God.
For all who were confirmed this year, that they may live by the Spirit they received.
For people living in darkness, sadness or despair, that they may see the light of Christ in us.
For families affected by the monsoon rains, for safety and for help from their neighbours.
For our group, that our yes may be yes and our promises kept.
pm.close: Father, may our good works shine before others so that they may give glory to you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul had told the Corinthians he would visit them, and then he changed his plans. Some people immediately said: this man cannot be trusted; he says yes and no at the same time. Paul answers: my travel plans may change, but the message I preached never changes, because it is Jesus Christ, and in him it is always Yes (2 Corinthians 1:19).

For in him every one of God's promises is a Yes (2 Corinthians 1:20). Think of all God's promises in the Old Testament: a land, a descendant, a king, a new covenant, a new heart. In Jesus they are all fulfilled. He is God's great Yes to humanity. And at every Mass, when the priest lifts up the Body and Blood of Christ, we answer Amen. That Amen is our yes to God's Yes.

Paul also says that God has anointed us, put his seal on us and given us his Spirit in our hearts (2 Corinthians 1:21–22). At Baptism and Confirmation we were anointed with holy chrism and sealed with the gift of the Holy Spirit. A seal is a mark of ownership. We belong to God. The Spirit in us is like an advance payment, a first installment of the joy of heaven.

And Jesus tells us what that means in daily life: you are the salt of the earth; you are the light of the world (Matthew 5:13–14). Not: you should become. You are. A Christian who hides his faith is like a lamp under a basket. In these monsoon nights, when the power goes off, we know how precious one small lamp is. Let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven (Matthew 5:16). Amen.
kids: Children, what happens if you forget to put salt in the curry? It tastes flat! And what happens when the electricity goes off at night? Everyone looks for a lamp. Jesus said to his friends: you are salt, and you are light. That means a Christian child makes things better, like salt in food, and helps others see God's goodness, like a lamp in the dark. When you share, help, and speak kindly, you are shining Jesus' light!

intro: Theme: “In him it is always Yes.”
God's faithful Yes in Christ, the seal of the Spirit on the baptised, and the salt and light that must not be hidden.

sub: Our plans change; God's word does not.
q: God is not a human being, that he should lie, or a mortal, that he should change his mind. Has he promised, and will he not do it?
For in him every one of God's promises is a “Yes.” For this reason it is through him that we say the “Amen,” to the glory of God.
points.apply: Today keep one promise you have made to God or to someone in your family, without excuses.

sub: The chrism of Baptism and Confirmation.
The Spirit as a first installment.
q: I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.
But it is God who establishes us with you in Christ and has anointed us, by putting his seal on us and giving us his Spirit in our hearts as a first installment.
points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and Confirmation and thank God for them on those days each year.

sub: A gift before it is a task.
A lamp on the stand, glory to the Father.
q: The unfolding of your words gives light; it imparts understanding to the simple.
You are the salt of the earth; but if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored?
points.apply: This week, do one good work openly in your parish or neighbourhood, and give the credit to God.

concl: In Jesus Christ every promise of God is Yes, and through him we answer Amen; by the Spirit we are anointed and sealed as God's own.
Jesus calls his disciples salt and light, and asks that our good works shine so that the Father may be glorified.
2027-06-08.resolve: Let your yes be faithful and your light visible: one kept promise and one good work each day this week.
